rubric.search_query:
Find candidates for this role:
Regulatory systems engineering role supporting NRC licensing for a portable nuclear microreactor. Own license-application deliverables, coordinate engineering inputs and regulator interactions, and integrate analysis and test results into regulatory submissions.
Mandatory professional qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in nuclear engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, or a similar technical field.
- 2+ years of experience certifying, regulating, qualifying, or auditing hardware that was manufactured, deployed, and iteratively improved.
- Applied understanding of requirements derivation, negotiation, and verification OR experience with the product-design process, especially defining systems, interfaces, and specifications.
Preferred, not mandatory:
- 5+ years of experience working in a manufacturing environment with strict regulatory oversight.
- Experience working on a nuclear project with DOE or NRC regulation.
- Experience tailoring or implementing NQA-1, ISO9001, AS9100, or other industrial standards.
- Experience owning, designing, building, or testing hardware that has seen production.
- Ability to apply fundamental engineering principles to regulatory efforts.
- Project management experience driving schedules forward.
- Ability to write technical documentation.
Work location and geographic eligibility:
Location: Greater Los Angeles area, California. Onsite work is based in this area, and candidates must currently be located in it. Specific cities and metropolitan areas also include any location within about 100 miles (160 km) of them; states, countries, and regions require a location inside them.
